one_line: proposed_change stops one kind of forbidden change before merge: a diff that edits the protective test file. With Docker up after KS-6b it also stops a diff that makes the test fail, which CI already catches. It cannot catch the critique's second door, and it fails open in five cases: skip, xfail, a conftest or pytest.toml change, Docker down, and any inconclusive. The same §3.4 paragraph says a changed blob means both PRESENT and inconclusive, and on the history every change to that blob was a legitimate edit (3 of 3).

attacks.attack: 1. Critique's example: a new file adds a known-device login path that mints a JWT and never calls the lock check. Which mechanism catches it, and when?
attacks.evidence:
Both protective tests call only the login entry points. test_service.py:102-132 drives IdentityService.login, and test_identity_integration.py:86-104 drives POST /api/auth/login. A new file leaves both test blobs unchanged, and the tests still pass. Under KS-O12 that is not_applies on both halves. The adjudicator recorded the same in critique-2026-11-03/verdicts.txt:44.
KS-O10 matches only identifiers. create_access_token appears 0 times in either protective test (grep -c) and is not on a changed line of the presumed fix 1c546a3. verify_pin appears only in test_service.py (3 times) and in one changed line of 1c546a3. A device path that mints a token without verifying a PIN therefore matches no derived ident handle. It fires only if the KS-4 author hand-adds create_access_token.
The only deterministic catch is D17's caller-pin pytest, run in CI on the PR. D17 is written only 'when ex6 is verified' (§11 D17, line 715; KS-6b deliverables). KS-6b runs only after a KS-5 go, and go-minimal or stop skip it entirely.
P7b-1 builds this exact door: w2/O-05-design.md item 4, 'known-device bypass'. Its Scope also forces edits to both protective files: roster removal (test_roster_lists_active_without_pins at integration:71) and set_pin requiring the current PIN (integration:143, 193). Any blob 'catch' at P7b-1 would come from that test-file churn, not from the door.
Worse, the --diff warning card says the fix stays withheld 'until ks verify --target proposed returns applies' (§4.1 step 4). That verify returns not_applies here, which an agent reads as clearance.
§7.2 is literally conditional ('a do-not-apply entry that verifies'). §5.5 and §9 (line 522) state this blind spot honestly. §12.7 files KS-O12 under point 2's 'brute-force throttling removed' harm without saying it never covers the second door.
attacks.consequence:
Answer to 'which mechanism':
- KS-O12: never catches this case.
- KS-O10: catches it at first commit, PR-ready and the KS-O11 review step only if ex6's ident handles name create_access_token; that is an author choice and not derivable.
- D17: catches it in CI on the PR, but only if D17 exists before P7b-1.
Required changes:
- Render proposed-mode not_applies for do_not_apply as inconclusive(protective_test_passes_coverage_unknown), on the KS-F11 pattern, never as clearance.
- Require create_access_token and verify_pin as author-named ident handles on ex6.
- Decouple D17's caller pin from ex6's verification (owner call).

attacks.attack: 2. Delete, rename, skip, xfail or rewrite the protective test's assertions. Which do the blob rule and the fails rule each catch, and what comes back when the test is missing from the proposed tree?
attacks.evidence:
'The test fails against the proposed change' catches none of the five. Each one makes the test not fail by construction:
- pytest junitxml.py append_skipped writes <skipped type="pytest.skip"> for a skip and <skipped type="pytest.xfail"> for a failing xfail test, never <failure>. So the present_when rule (fail in the call phase with a matching reprcrash, line 267) reads ABSENT.
- Rewritten assertions pass, so ABSENT.
- Delete or rename: pytest raises UsageError('not found: ...'), which maps to ExitCode.USAGE_ERROR (exit 4 per the exit-codes page), and KS-6b's fault list sends a renamed test to inconclusive.
'The blob differs from the approved one' catches all five. But §3.4 line 275 gives that same condition two verdicts in one paragraph: 'the protective test's blob must equal the approved one or the verdict is inconclusive (critic K12)' and 'PRESENT means ... or the protective test's blob differs from the approved one' (KS-O12). KS-6b (line 636) repeats K12's inconclusive. KS-3 (line 592) expects applies. So whether the five stop depends on which sentence the implementer reads.
Neither skipped nor xfail appears anywhere in the design (grep).
attacks.consequence:
Resolve the contradiction explicitly (see amendments).
Add junit <skipped> of either type, XPASS and exit 4 to the protective-test outcomes, mapping each to protection_disabled. That is a stop for do_not_apply, never ABSENT.

attacks.attack: 3. A conftest.py or pytest report-hook change on the proposed tree. Is inconclusive treated as no stop?
attacks.evidence:
Yes. §4.1 step 5 (line 304) says 'inconclusive behaves as a miss and escalates', and §7.2 (line 445) stops only an entry that 'verifies'. So inconclusive does not stop.
It is worse than inconclusive: several routes return a clean not_applies.
- A precondition that differs does not cap the verdict. Only an unprobed precondition caps at inconclusive; a differing one 'blocks reaffirmed' (line 277).
- The repository's own backend/tests/conftest.py:65-72 already defines pytest_collection_modifyitems, which turns integration tests into skips when FIXFLOW_TEST_DATABASE_URL is unset. A collection hook is not one of the named report hooks, so a skip produced through it reads ABSENT.
- test_service.py has no conftest on its path at all. git ls-files shows only backend/tests/conftest.py and backend/app/features/jobs/tests/conftest.py. A newly added conftest therefore has no recorded blob to differ from.
- pytest's customize page: pytest.toml or .pytest.toml 'always match, even if empty', and pytest.ini takes precedence over pyproject.toml. pyproject allows pytest>=8.3,<10.0. A new empty pytest.toml silently replaces backend/pyproject.toml:55-62 (asyncio_mode, pythonpath, testpaths, markers) without touching any conftest or test blob.
- pyproject.toml has 27 commits on main; conftest.py has 11.
attacks.consequence:
For a do_not_apply entry in proposed_change mode, every inconclusive must stop, routing to the phase's Opus reviewer: fail closed, consistent with KS-O9's recall-first rule.
The precondition set becomes the conftest set on the test's path, with absence recorded, plus the pytest config-file set and .gitattributes. Any change to it stops as protection_changed.

attacks.attack: 4. Docker not running, or before KS-6b. What does verify --target proposed return, and is inconclusive no stop?
attacks.evidence:
Before KS-6b the pytest kind does not exist: its executable half is KS-6b's (line 275, line 636). KS-6a says 'Docker stopped yields sandbox_unavailable', and §9 says Docker Desktop does not auto-start, so test-id checks are 'usually inconclusive'. ex6 is unverified_seed until KS-6 (§8 rule 1).
The only live signal is the KS-3 blob comparison. For an A2 patch that leaves the tests alone, the blob is equal and the executable half is inconclusive, so nothing stops. CI's own test_service.py run catches that patch instead.
It is unverifiable whether an 'approved blob' exists for ex6 before KS-6b. Approval binds to spec_sha for executable kinds, and ex6's control pair is first demonstrated in KS-6b.
attacks.consequence:
State in §3.4 and §9 that before KS-6b, and whenever Docker is down, proposed_change means only that the diff touched the protective-test or config set.
Under the fail-closed rule, sandbox_unavailable on a do_not_apply verify stops pending a reviewer ruling. It does not pass.

attacks.attack: 5. What declarative check can a do_not_apply entry have? Can KS-5 exercise proposed_change beyond blob equality?
attacks.evidence:
ex6 has no declarative probe. KS-F7 (line 271) forbids any text probe from returning applies on a code-behaviour entry, and KS-O1 (line 272) builds no span anchoring before KS-6b.
KS-3's 'blob and span comparison' (line 592) therefore reduces to whole-file blob equality. The 'span' half contradicts KS-O1, and no verdict is defined for a changed protected span.
The blob rule also fails the design's own write gate. Its mandatory specificity controls say 'passes_at plus semantics-preserving refactor mutants (file move, comment edit ...) must still read ABSENT' (line 275). A comment edit or a file move changes the blob, so the rule reads PRESENT and is refused at write time.
KS-5's diff arm (line 614) replays only `ks lookup --diff`. It never runs verify --target proposed. Its one ex6 synthetic diff ('A2's patch with the two protective tests inverted') is exactly the case blob equality catches by construction.
attacks.consequence:
Say plainly that the KS-5 pilot cannot exercise proposed_change beyond blob equality, and that the KS-5 go criterion says nothing about KS-O12.
Add verify --target proposed to the diff arm. Add the A2-alone, second-door, skip, xfail, conftest and pytest.toml diffs, plus replays of 2f48529 and 1c546a3 scored as legitimate edits that must be reported if they stop.
Exempt the blob guard from refactor-mutant controls on the ground that it never returns applies.

attacks.attack: 6. The rule 'fix withheld until applies' against a do_not_apply entry whose value is its reason. What does show print, and what is released or withheld?
attacks.evidence:
Only the `fix` field is withheld (§7.1 line 433). 'Dead ends' are 'shown under an UNVERIFIED banner even on a candidate'. architect-A puts ex6's reason into negatives (the A2 prescription as worse_side_effect with the attack math; inverting the tests as wrong_premise), and cause and diagnosis are not withheld.
So the reason is reachable without PRESENT, and the critic's premise 'the reason ... was withheld' holds only for the `fix` field.
When PRESENT does release it, it goes to whichever agent of any tier ran verify. That is harmless, because a do_not_apply 'fix' is a prohibition.
What is wrong is withholding it at all. In the second-door case verify never returns applies, so the prohibition line stays withheld for good, and the warning card names only 'the entry and the protected span' (§4.1 step 4).
attacks.consequence:
Do not withhold the fix of a do_not_apply entry, since the withholding rationale inverts for a prohibition.
Put the one-line prohibition on the --diff warning card inside the 2,000-character cap.

attacks.attack: 7. Approver-is-not-author for the protective-test blob, and a later legitimate test edit.
attacks.evidence:
The text never says who approves the protective-test blob or whether its OID is inside spec_sha. Approval binds approved_by ≠ author to spec_sha for executable kinds (line 267), and identity is self-declared (§5.3, §9).
At solve time (§7.3) the entry author can also write the protective test. The PR reviewer then approves both, which is allowed but is only policy.
History on origin/main:
- test_identity_integration.py changed blob after its lock test existed (2f48529^ line 80) in 2f48529, an unrelated phase (integrity FKs, 0032), which edited a different test at line 144 (blob 649c2fc to 0ae4bf1).
- 1c546a3 (#169), the legitimate lockout fix, changed both protective files.
- So 3 of 3 post-introduction blob changes were legitimate and 0 were forbidden.
P7b-1 must change both files (roster removal; set_pin needs the current PIN). Each such edit leaves every later ex6 verify either PRESENT (KS-O12; tree mode then says 'forbidden change already on the target') or inconclusive (K12) in every later phase.
That contradicts §7.2's rule that --diff 'compares against the diff and never the stored trace (an unrelated change merged earlier does not keep firing)'.
No re-approval path exists in §7.4 or anywhere else (grep for re-approv/reapprov/approved blob returned nothing).
attacks.consequence:
Add a re-approval path: when a PR changes a do_not_apply protective blob and the reviewer rules it legitimate, the reviewer runs ks revise binding the new blob, a second Opus runs ks approve, and the inject-control is re-shown on the new blob, all in the same review.
Until then the tree-mode verdict is inconclusive(protection_changed_unapproved), never applies, and ks close reports it as such, never as 'regression'.

attacks.attack: 8. Is proposed_change well-defined for the three targets? Can the forbidden change hide in an untracked file or a submodule?
attacks.evidence:
Targets:
- §7.1 (line 432) gives `--target proposed --diff <merge-base>`, and §3.4 adds '(or the working tree)', with no flag to choose between them.
- The blob rule compares against the approved blob, not the merge-base, so the merge-base argument plays no part in the declarative half.
Untracked files:
- `git stash create` omits untracked files (KS-F19), and refusal triggers only when an untracked path matches the footprint or probe path set. An untracked new conftest or pytest.toml is not in that set.
- It is also absent from the snapshot, so it fools the gate only once committed, and the HEAD mode then sees it. That part holds.
Submodules and archive attributes:
- The repository has no .gitmodules (git ls-files).
- The KS-6a sandbox is fed by git archive. Per the git-archive docs, export-ignore is honoured from 'the .gitattributes files in the tree that is being archived'. A proposed .gitattributes line can drop the protective test from the sandbox while `git rev-parse <rev>:<path>` still shows the approved blob. The result is not found, inconclusive and no stop.
Ordering on the prescription route:
- §7.2 (line 445) runs the lookup and verify 'before applying'. At that moment the proposed tree equals the base, so verify returns not_applies and the stop cannot fire.
- It can fire only on the later --diff route (PR-ready, the reviewer), that is before merge, not before the edit.
Inject-control:
- §5.2 (line 343) re-demonstrates controls 'on the target', and §4.3 (line 315) turns a failed flip into a controls_broken event, which is journaled and demotes the entry to suspect for every session.
- A proposed tree that inverted or skipped the test makes the injected A2 mutant read ABSENT. So the very change under review demotes ex6 globally, and the verdict pre-empts KS-O12's PRESENT.
attacks.consequence:
Use `--target proposed[=head|worktree]`, comparing against both the merge-base and the approved blob.
Add .gitattributes to the protected config set.
In proposed mode, demonstrate the controls on the base. A failed inject-control on the proposed tree is the protection_disabled stop and never writes controls_broken.
A doc_ref exact hit on a do_not_apply entry stops by itself, and verify runs after the edit.

attacks.evidence:
release/drain is cut at P1's squash commit (SHIP-PLAN lines 66-73), probably before tools/ks exists, so the rule 'ks missing → phase proceeds' (§7.6) applies there. Only drain-tool fixes are cherry-picked onto it, so identity changes are unlikely.
The global controls_broken from attack 8 is the real parallel-session hazard. Its frequency needs the store.

counter_evidence:
1. The paragraph contradicts itself. §3.4, line 275 of the design, gives one condition two verdicts: K12 says a protective test whose blob differs from the approved one makes the verdict inconclusive, and KS-O12, in the same paragraph, says it makes the verdict PRESENT. KS-6b (line 636) restates inconclusive, while KS-3 (line 592) expects applies.

2. The blob rule cannot pass the design's own controls. KS-F7's mandatory refactor mutants (a comment edit or a file move must read ABSENT, line 275) change the blob. So the rule reads PRESENT where ABSENT is required and is refused at write time.

3. History shows only false stops. On origin/main, every post-introduction blob change to the protective files was legitimate. 2f48529 edited the integration test file for an unrelated FK change (blob 649c2fc to 0ae4bf1). 1c546a3 was the correct lockout fix. P7b-1 must edit both files. That is 3 of 3 legitimate and 0 forbidden.

4. Five changes defeat 'the test fails'. pytest's junitxml writes skip and xfail as <skipped>, never <failure>, so the test never reads PRESENT:
- a skip marker;
- an xfail marker;
- the repository's existing pytest_collection_modifyitems skip hook (backend/tests/conftest.py:65-72);
- a new conftest where none exists today (test_service.py has none on its path);
- a new empty pytest.toml, which per pytest's docs outranks pyproject.toml.
None of these is named in the KS-6b fault list.

5. Inconclusive never stops. Per §4.1 step 5 it 'behaves as a miss'; §7.2 stops only an entry that 'verifies'; KS-6a returns sandbox_unavailable when Docker is down.

6. The second door goes through. A known-device file that mints a JWT is not_applies on both halves, which the adjudication itself recorded (verdicts.txt:44). It matches no derived ident handle, because create_access_token appears in neither protective test. Only D17 catches it, and D17 is gated behind KS-6b.

7. The prescription route verifies too early. That verify runs before the edit exists, so it returns not_applies.

8. Inject-control on a proposed tree demotes the guard globally. Re-demonstrating controls on a proposed tree that has disabled the test writes a journaled controls_broken event, which makes ex6 suspect for every session.

amendments.section: §3.4 (the test_id bullet, KS-O12 and K12 sentences)
amendments.change:
Replace both clauses with one rule.

In target_mode proposed_change a do_not_apply check has these outcomes:
- `applies`: the protective test, with its blob equal to the approved one, fails in the call phase against the proposed tree.
- `stop(protection_changed)`: the diff changes any of these:
  - the protective test's blob;
  - any conftest.py on its path, including adding one where none existed;
  - the pytest config-file set (pytest.toml, .pytest.toml, pytest.ini, pyproject [tool.pytest*], tox.ini, setup.cfg);
  - .gitattributes.
- `stop(protection_disabled)` (from KS-6b): either the stored forbidden mutant, injected into the proposed tree, no longer makes the protective test fail, or junit reports the test as <skipped> of any type, XPASS, or not found (exit 4 or 5).
- `inconclusive(<reason>)`: for a do_not_apply entry in proposed_change mode this also stops until the phase's Opus reviewer rules.
- A passing protective test renders as `inconclusive(protective_test_passes_coverage_unknown)`, never as not_applies or clearance (the KS-F11 pattern).

In target_mode tree, a blob differing from the approved one is `inconclusive(protection_changed_unapproved)`, never applies.

The blob and config-set comparison is a guard on the check's input, not a probe. It never returns applies, so KS-F7's refactor-mutant controls do not apply to it.
amendments.why: The same paragraph currently gives the same condition two verdicts (K12: inconclusive; KS-O12: PRESENT). As a probe, the blob rule fails KS-F7's mandatory comment-edit and file-move mutants. On main, 3 of 3 blob changes were legitimate. Skip and xfail are written as <skipped>, so they read ABSENT. And inconclusive never stops.

amendments.change: In proposed_change mode the controls are demonstrated on the base (the merge-base, or the tree holding the approved blob), never on the proposed tree. A failed inject-control on the proposed tree is the protection_disabled stop of §3.4. It never writes controls_broken and never changes status.
amendments.why: Otherwise a diff that inverts or skips the protective test writes a journaled controls_broken event. That event demotes ex6 for every session, and the gate returns inconclusive before KS-O12's PRESENT is reached.

amendments.section: §7.2 (Before applying a fix that a prose register prescribes)
amendments.change: Replace 'a do-not-apply entry that verifies in proposed_change mode stops the change' with this. A `doc_ref` or `--prescription` exact hit on a do_not_apply entry stops the change by itself until the phase's Opus reviewer rules. `ks verify --target proposed=worktree` is re-run after the edit is written, and 'before the change lands' means before merge.
amendments.why: Verify run 'before applying' compares a proposed tree equal to the base, so it returns not_applies and the stop cannot fire on this route.

amendments.change: Write the target as `--target proposed[=head|worktree] --diff <merge-base>`. Spell out that the protection_changed guard compares the proposed tree with both the merge-base and the approved blob, and stops only when the diff itself changes the protected set.
amendments.why: Today the merge-base plays no part in the blob rule. An earlier legitimate merge (for example 2f48529) would then make every later proposed verify stop, which contradicts §7.2's 'never the stored trace' rule.

amendments.change: Add a re-approval path. When a PR changes a do_not_apply entry's protective test or its config set and the PR's Opus reviewer rules the change legitimate, the reviewer, being a non-author, runs `ks revise` binding the new blob OIDs. A second Opus session runs `ks approve --spec-sha` after re-showing the inject-control (the new test still fails under the stored forbidden mutant), in the same review. Until then `ks close` reports the entry as 'protection changed, unapproved', never as 'regression'.
amendments.why: P7b-1 must edit both of ex6's protective files (roster removal; set_pin needs the current PIN), and the text has no path that restores a usable verdict afterwards.

amendments.change: Fix withholding does not apply to do_not_apply entries. Their `fix` is a prohibition and is printed on any card. The --diff warning card carries the entry's one-line prohibition inside the 2,000-character cap.
amendments.why: Withholding a prohibition is the fail-open direction. In the second-door case verify never returns applies, so the prohibition is never released.
The only ex6 synthetic diff today (A2 with the tests inverted) is the one case blob equality catches by construction, and the arm never runs verify --target proposed.
Today's list (exit 127, exit 5, a renamed test, a conftest import error, a report hook, a beforeEach throw) misses every route that turns the protective test into a skip or deselects it.

amendments.change: Name `create_access_token` and `verify_pin` as author-named `ident` handles on ex6. Make D17's caller-pin pytest independent of ex6's verification and of the KS-5 verdict: it is repository CI and needs no store, so it can land any time before P7b-1 (owner ruling).
amendments.why: create_access_token is absent from both protective tests and from 1c546a3's changed lines, so it is not derivable. D17 is the only mechanism that catches the critique's example, and today it exists only after KS-6b, which runs only on a KS-5 go.

amendments.change: Narrow 'returns PRESENT when the protective test fails against the proposed change or its blob differs from the approved one' to the four-outcome rule above. Add that KS-O12 never covers a second door the protective test does not drive. That case is D17's, and KS-O10's only if ex6's ident handles name the minted-token call.
amendments.why: As written, the ruling implies the stop rule fires before any forbidden change lands, but it fires only for test-file edits (from KS-3) and for diffs that make the test fail (from KS-6b, with Docker up).

changes_a_127_ruling:
This changes KS-O12. Its clause 'PRESENT when ... its blob differs from the approved one' becomes a stop pending the reviewer's ruling. It is not applies in proposed mode and is inconclusive in tree mode, which also resolves the clash with K12.

Further changes to the KS-O12 rule:
- Inconclusive in proposed mode stops a do_not_apply entry.
- A passing protective test reads inconclusive(coverage_unknown), not not_applies.
- Controls are demonstrated on the base, never on the proposed tree.

Two related rulings change:
- KS-O14: its synthetic diff set grows and the arm gains verify --target proposed.
- KS-O6 / D17: decoupled from ex6's KS-6b verification.

The point-2 ruling's 'lets the stop rule fire before the change lands' is narrowed to: before merge, and only for test-file edits or test-failing diffs.
could_not_run: The gate on its own terms, because the store does not exist: no tools/ks, no store, no index. That rules out `ks verify --target proposed`, the inject-control and controls_broken behaviour, and any verdict a combination of half-results would give.

Running ex6's protective tests against proposed trees. This needs Docker (not running), the backend's Python dependencies (not installed) and pytest (absent from the bundled interpreter). Running them inside the repository would also write __pycache__ and .pytest_cache there.
Measuring the junit output for skip and xfail on this box (no pytest). The primary source used instead is pytest's junitxml.py append_skipped.
Whether ex6 has an approved protective-test blob before KS-6b, and which ident handles its KS-4 author would name.
The real false-stop rate of the blob rule beyond main's history: P7b-1 has not been written.
